lead: A whole month of festivities in midsummer. Concerts under the stars in Viveros, fireworks every Saturday, the Jazz Festival, the Band Competition and the Battle of Flowers as a spectacular grand finale.

The Gran Feria de Julio is the festival of the Valencian summer: a whole month of activities that fill squares, gardens, theatres and beaches with concerts, shows, fireworks and traditions. Unlike the Fallas — concentrated in 19 days in March — the Gran Feria unfolds at a steadier pace, with big nights alternating with neighbourhood-by-neighbourhood programming.

Most street events are completely free. Only the big concerts at Viveros and some Jazz Festival performances charge admission. The rest — fireworks, Battle of Flowers, Gran Nit de Juliol, Band Competition, magic, circus and open-air dances — are for everyone.

items.title: Viveros Concerts
items.subtitle: The big musical event of the summer · Pop, rock, flamenco, rap · Night after night
items.body: The Viveros Concerts are the musical highlight of the Gran Feria and one of the most popular open-air summer festivals in Spain. For almost the whole month of July, the Jardines del Real — popularly known as Viveros — become the stage for Spanish and international pop, rock, flamenco and rap artists. The venue fills night after night with tens of thousands of people under the stars, in one of the prettiest settings in Valencia. Each year the line-up surprises with a mix of big names and new talent. The atmosphere of the lit-up gardens, with the centuries-old pines in the background and the heat of the Valencian summer, makes every concert a memorable experience.
facts: Jardines del Real (Viveros) · 1 to 25 July · Paid admission · Check the line-up at granferiavalencia.com

items.title: Firework Displays
items.subtitle: A different pyrotechnic firm every Saturday · CAC, Monteolivete Bridge, Plaza del Ayuntamiento
items.body: Every Saturday in July, at 23:59, the Valencia sky lights up with spectacular firework displays fired from different points of the city. Each week a different pyrotechnic firm signs its show, creating a healthy rivalry that raises the quality of each night. The best places to watch are the Turia Garden, the Alameda promenade and the Monteolivete bridge, with the City of Arts and Sciences in the background. The climax comes with the final pyromusical display — the “Mar d’Estiu” — which closes the Gran Feria with hundreds of kilos of gunpowder in a show of more than 20 minutes.
facts: Every Saturday in July · 23:59 · Different points of the city · Free access

items.title: Valencia Jazz Festival
items.subtitle: 120+ years of history · Free concerts · Jam sessions · International artists
items.body: The Valencia Jazz Festival opens the Gran Feria each year with one of the events most loved by Valencians. With more than 120 years of history, it brings together the best national and international jazz performers at the Palau de la Música and at open-air venues across the city. The opening concert in the Jardines del Palau is especially anticipated and usually free. The legendary jam sessions in the bars and squares of the centre, where musicians improvise until the small hours, are the festival’s most authentic soul and a great plan for early July nights.
facts: First half of July · Palau de la Música and urban venues
First half of July · Palau de la Música + urban venues · Concerts from €5–20 and free

items.title: International Band Competition · “Ciudad de Valencia”
items.subtitle: More than a century of competition · Bands from all over Spain and Europe
items.body: The “Ciudad de Valencia” International Band Competition is one of the most prestigious and longest-running band contests in Spain, with more than a century of history. For several days in mid-July, the Palau de la Música hosts the performances of the participating bands, divided into different sections, which compete before a specialist jury. Many of them are Valencian bands, a tradition deeply rooted in the musical culture of the Comunitat Valenciana. Both the competition concerts and the performances by guest bands are of exceptional musical standard and very affordable admission.
facts: 15–19 July · Palau de la Música · Check the programme at granferiavalencia.com

items.title: Gran Nit de Juliol
items.subtitle: 30+ venues · Museums open free · Pyromusical show · Paella and culture
items.body: The Gran Nit de Juliol is the most cross-cutting night of the Gran Feria: a day when the whole city becomes an enormous stage of free culture. More than 30 points spread across squares, gardens and neighbourhoods simultaneously host concerts, circus shows, theatre, magic, dance and storytelling. Valencia’s museums open their doors at night and free of charge, allowing night-time visits with special activities. The night culminates in a grand pyromusical show at the Monteolivete Bridge at 00:30. The Parque Central, the Plaza de la Virgen, the Plaza del Ayuntamiento and the Jardines del Palau are the liveliest venues.
facts: One Saturday in July · The whole city · Museums open until the small hours
One Saturday in July · The whole city · Free museums · Pyromusical 00:30 at Monteolivete

items.title: Battle of Flowers
items.subtitle: Since 1891 · 1,200,000 carnations · 30+ floats · The grand finale of the fair
items.body: The Battle of Flowers is the spectacular climax of the Gran Feria and one of Valencia’s best-loved traditions since 1891. On the last Sunday of July, more than 30 floats decorated with flowers parade along the Paseo de la Alameda while their crews throw more than 1,200,000 carnations to the public. For nearly an hour, hundreds of thousands of flowers fly through the air in all directions, until at the end the Alameda is covered by an impressive multicoloured carpet of petals. The smell of flowers mixed with the heat of the Valencian summer is unmistakable. The Battle of Flowers is a visual and sensory event with no comparison in any other Spanish festival.
facts: Last Sunday in July · 20:00 · Paseo de la Alameda
Last Sunday in July · Paseo de la Alameda · 20:00 · Free access · Since 1891

items.title: Funfair, Magic and More
items.subtitle: Rides in the Turia · Magic shows · Moors and Christians · Albufera visits
items.body: The Gran Feria fills the whole of July with a parallel programme that goes far beyond the big events. The Funfair is set up in the Turia Garden between the Puente de las Flores and the Puente de la Exposición, with a Ferris wheel, swing rides and attractions for all ages. Family magic shows tour markets, squares and streets. In El Cabanyal, the Moors and Christians parade recreates historic battles. From Monday to Wednesday there are free guided visits to the Albufera at sunset. And in the neighbourhoods and outlying districts, each day brings concerts, storytelling, circus and neighbourhood open-air dances that are the most authentic Feria.

blocks.title: Tips for enjoying the Gran Feria
items: For the Battle of Flowers arrive 1 hour early at the Paseo de la Alameda and get a front-row spot — the carnations are thrown straight at you
The Viveros Concerts sell out: buy tickets in advance at granferiavalencia.com as soon as the line-up is announced
The Gran Nit de Juliol is free — note down the museums you want to visit at night because they fill up fast
The Saturday fireworks can be seen perfectly from the Turia Garden and the Paseo de la Alameda — without fighting for a spot
The opening Jazz Festival concert in the Jardines del Palau is usually free — it is the most elegant plan of the whole fair
The Turia Funfair is open until August — perfect for hot afternoons with children by the river
